campaign.title: DC2 Research Program A — Cross-Asset Transition Ecology

origin.motivation: Understand cross-asset information propagation before XAU/USD regime transitions.

research_question_primary.title: Cross-Asset Transition Ecology — Primary Research Question
research_question_primary.motivation: Determine how cross-asset markets create, amplify, or suppress XAU/USD regime transitions.

research_questions_secondary.statement: Which markets consistently lead XAU/USD in the governed dataset?
Which markets consistently lag XAU/USD in the governed dataset?
Which cross-asset relationships change by regime?
Which cross-asset relationships disappear during stress?
Which markets dominate during macro transitions?
Which relationships are causal versus merely correlated?
Do cross-asset relationships evolve over time (adaptive markets)?
What signals propagate information about impending XAU/USD regime transitions?

experiments.title: Theme 1 — Cross-Asset Lead-Lag Analysis
experiments.description: Cross-correlation at lags -20 to +20 days between XAU/USD returns and each governed cross-asset signal. Regime-conditioned profiles computed for four key signals.

experiments.title: Theme 2 — Information Flow Analysis
experiments.description: Transfer entropy proxy via binned mutual information at lags 1-20 days. Granger causality proxy via OLS R-squared gain. Regime-conditioned mutual information for all six regimes.

experiments.title: Theme 3 — Transition Ecology Analysis
experiments.description: Identification of all regime transitions in the governed frame. Window analysis of signal behavior at offsets w-10 to w+10 days relative to transitions. Dominant pre-transition signal ranking.

experiments.title: Theme 4 — Market Synchronization Analysis
experiments.description: Rolling 60-day correlation analysis stratified by normal, stress, geopolitical, and calendar-event periods. Regime-conditioned synchronization. Cross-signal correlation matrix.

experiments.title: Theme 5 — Adaptive Behaviour Analysis
experiments.description: Rolling 252-day correlations with stability scoring. Epoch comparison (early vs late sample) with structural change detection. Sign-flip rate as regime-adaptive marker.

entity.title: Cross-Asset Transition Ecology — Primary Research Question
